title: The Copper Regiment
premise: In the winter of 1799, Silas Lockridge carries sealed dispatches aboard the copper-sheathed frigate Meridian, bound for a colonial governor whose republic is collapsing behind it. When a census taker boarding at port recognizes the cipher in Silas's satchel, Silas must hide among the ship's ragtag crew — a found family of deserters, debtors, and dreamers — while deciding whether to deliver documents that will doom them all. The final berth on the returning convoy holds room for only one: his blood brother, who betrayed him to the census taker, or Wren, the young deckhand who has become his true family. Silas gives the berth to Wren, delivers the dispatches unopened to their rightful rebel hands instead, and stays behind as the century turns — no longer a courier, but home.
about_author: Casper Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing merchant ship manifests from the 1790s. They write historical fiction about the quiet people history forgot to count.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Aboard the Meridian at Port Calloway, Silas keeps his head down repairing rigging until a census taker named Mr. Quill boards and asks each man his name, trade, and birthplace. At Silas's turn, Quill lingers on one extra question about papers carried. Silas lies smoothly, but that night he finds his satchel disturbed. Beat: dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Copper Bottom, Iron Men
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The young deckhand introduces the crew: gruff Bosun Adeyemi, exiled surgeon Madame Voss, and the brothers Tam and Rill. Wren idolizes the quiet new hand who fixes things without being asked. We see the Meridian as a floating village of people escaping pasts. Beat: warmth and belonging taking root.

chapters.title: What the Satchel Holds
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Flashback reveals the dispatches: surrender terms that would hand the colony's rebels to the crown, entrusted to him by his dying handler — his own brother Edmund, who now serves the other side. Silas was meant to be a ghost courier. Instead he's begun to care whether these people live. Beat: divided heart.

chapters.title: The Counting House
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. The census taker writes coded reports of his own; he suspects the courier is aboard and believes turning him in will buy his family passage off the doomed colony. His chapters humanize the antagonist: a father doing arithmetic with other men's lives. Beat: sympathy for the hunter.

chapters.title: Storm Glass
chapters.summary: Adeyemi's POV. A hurricane forces all hands together; Silas saves Rill from being swept overboard, cementing his place in the crew's trust. But in the aftermath, Tam finds Silas's cipher wheel washed loose from the wreckage and says nothing — yet. Beat: loyalty deepening, secret surfacing.

chapters.title: Brother's Keeper
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At mid-voyage port, Silas discovers Edmund is stationed there, wearing an officer's coat. Their reunion is tender and poisonous: Edmund offers Silas redemption, a berth home, and forgiveness — if he surrenders the dispatches. Silas refuses, not yet knowing Edmund has already written to Quill. Beat: betrayal dressed as love.

chapters.title: The Long Middle Watch
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Tam confronts Silas privately; instead of exposing him, Silas tells the truth, and Tam chooses the crew over the crown. But Quill intercepts the letter Edmund sent and now knows everything. He offers the captain a bargain: the courier, or the whole crew censused and conscripted. Beat: the noose tightening around everyone.

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. News arrives: the returning convoy has exactly one civilian berth left before the colony falls. The crew votes — not on who goes, but on whether Silas should be given up. Wren speaks for him; Adeyemi casts the deciding silence. Then Silas learns Edmund has claimed the berth in his name. Beat: impossible choice crystallized.

chapters.title: The Turning of the Year
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. New Year's Eve, 1799. Silas trades himself to Quill to secure Wren's berth, then turns the tables: he opens the dispatches before the assembled officers, revealing Edmund forged the surrender terms for personal gain. Mutiny swells; Edmund is arrested by his own allies. As midnight bells ring, Silas stands on deck between two centuries, two families, two selves. Beat: climax — truth over loyalty to blood.

chapters.title: Counted
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Weeks later, the Meridian sails under new colors for the rebel provisional government. Quill, spared, records the crew honestly in his census — names, trades, birthplaces, and for the first time, chosen family noted beside blood. Silas remains, mending rigging, busy-handed, home. Final line echoes the opening question, answered differently. Beat: belonging earned and kept.
